product_title: Carhartt Men's Blended Twill Work Chino Pant B290
review_body:
When I ordered the Carhartt Men's Twill Work Pants, I wasn't sure how well I would like them. I have never owned Carhartt clothing before, so had no frame of reference for these pants. Boy, was I surprised! I knew Carhartt's reputation for building really tough clothing for outdoor work (I think farmers and loggers spending all day outside in harsh conditions). But as far as indoor work pants, this was new. I am SO GLAD I got them. The construction is superior to anything I have seen thus far. Dickies, as nice as they are, are not nearly as well made as these.
I work in the 'quick serve' (fast food) industry as a manager, so I am called on to do everything in the store - from cashiering to cooking, from prep to paperwork, I do it all! These pants are so rugged, I feel like I can do anything my restaurant requires of me with little thought as to what will happen to my clothes. The stain resistant/liquid repellent coating is excellent for rejecting water that is frequently splashed on me; and grease seems to have no effect on them (as far as clean up goes). These pants really are that good!
I now have 3 pair purchased through Amazon and will buy 2 more to round out my work wardrobe.
My only concerns with these pants are (as has been mentioned by other reviewers) 1. the lack of pocket depth. They skimped a bit on pockets with these pants, they are about an inch or so too shallow. One would expect them to think that real \\"workers\\" carry a good amount of junk in their pockets! And 2. The number of belt loops seems to vary from pant to pant. The first order I received (30 x 34) had 7 loops, pretty standard for pants these days. But the subsequent orders (30 x 32, and 28 x 32) only had 5 loops. One would think that a 30 inch waist is a 30 inch waist and should have 7 loops every time. I might see only 5 on a 28 inch waist due to it being so small, but come on! A couple extra loops makes a big difference in how they fit and feel (secure or less so) when worn.
Oh and a note to those who order from Carhartt, they tend to go a little large on their sizing. That's why my first pair was a 30 x 34, I have a little waist and long legs, but these are TOO long. Also the waist is \\"generous\\". My actual size (which is nearly impossible to find without tailoring is 29 x 33. So, most companies I order from offer 30 x 32 or 34, I usually go for the 30 x 34 and they work great. But they are a bit too loose from Carhartt, so I got the 28 x 32 and they fit 'snug' but comfortable and the length is spot on.

Every thing seems well attached and constructed very well, so I do heartily endorse these Carhartt work pants as being tough and comfortable for a full 10 hour work shift. Hope this review helps you in making your decision to purchase these pants. I don't think you'll be disappointed. Especially for the great price Amazon offers!!

product_title: Men's Dress Vest & BowTie Solid RED Color Bow Tie Set for Suit or Tuxedo
review_headline: Great purchasing experience; will definitely do business again!
review_body:
Let me start off by saying that this was my first ever purchase from Amazon, and let me say that the seller made it a great experience. I have separated my review into multiple categories, each with a 1 to 10 (best) rating.

SELLER COMMUNICATIONS (10/10):
Before buying, I had several questions, and not all at the same time. I contacted the seller three different times, and when I woke up the following morning, I had received a very helpful reply that answered my questions.

Shipping (10/10)
I ordered the vest on a Saturday, and I received it on the following Thursday and I only used standard/shipping. So unless it's a last second purchase, you don't need to spend the extra bucks on super fast shipping. Note that the company ships its products out from California near Los Angeles, and I live in the middle of the U.S., so if you live farther east, it might take an extra day.

Product (9/10)
I ordered the red vesuvio napoli vest with the bow tie for prom, but I'm sure all of them can be reviewed on the same basis with a different color. The material is 100% polyester; it has a nice feel to it. You don't have to worry about the material being thick as the picture may suggest. The two problems I have with the vest are: the tightening belt in the back is a little hard to use, and unless someone is helping you, it will be very difficult for you to do yourself. The other problem is that the buttons seem very light and you must treat them with care. These are definitely not made to be washed. Nevertheless, these two problems are very minimal.

Pricing (10/10)
Not only do you get the same vest that Men's Wearhouse will charge you $40 for, but you get a bow tie as well, which costs an extra $10 at Macy's, so this is a VERY good deal.

Sizing (10/10)
If you are wondering about sizing, I can tell you that I am 5'10, 135 pounds, and I ordered the large, at first it does seem large/baggy, but then you remember the tightening belt in the back and then all is well.

Overall (10/10)
If you need a tuxedo vest for prom or a wedding, I really recommend the Vesuvio Napoli brand. An amazing product for an amazing price; I will definitely be doing business again.Overall (10/10) If you need a tuxedo vest for prom or a wedding, I really recommend the Vesuvio Napoli brand. review_headline: Wanted to love it - not for shallow breasts
review_body:
I have been breastfeeding for 7 years continuously as of this writing. It was (long past) time for some new bras. After carefully measuring (34DDD/E) and researching the huge variety of bras available, I decided to try this one based on reviews both here and from friends. I really wanted to love this bra like so many others but I had to return it.

Loved:
Material is soft and very comfortable. Band measurement was right on and band never cut into me (wore for about 1/2 a day). Clasps are strong yet easy to undo and reconnect one-handed. Removable pads for discretion and leaks also conceal nursing pads.

Didnt love:
Cups are not very supportive. This is great for many but not for shallow breasted women who need lots of lower support. Wearing this, my breasts drooped way over the band -causing it to fold in half- and looked awful. The pads helped cover nipples and did add some support when placed low but only gave me a tube-boob look. Without the pads, nursing pads show clearly.

Photos are with and without pads. Photo without the pads also shows the folded band.

product_title: DC Comics Deluxe Batgirl Adult Costume
review_headline: If you want the pictured item, purchase the one shipped and sold by Amazon!
review_body:
It seems a lot of the costume companies can't be trusted to list their items on Amazon correctly. There are different versions of this costume, and many of the reviews state they didn't receive the exact costume as pictured. I had ordered the American Dream costume (through Official Costumes), and while the picture advertised looked great, what I received was sub par. I called the company, and thankfully, they'll be paying for the return... as they should, considering I paid for the pictured costume and not some cheaper version. They were also very polite when I called, to give them credit. I decided to order this Batgirl costume since the other one didn't work out, and at another reviewer's suggestion I purchased the one that was shipped and sold by Amazon. It arrived two days ago and is exactly as pictured!

For reference, I'm 5'7\\", 136 pounds, 34DD (37\\" across the bust), 28.5\\" waist, and 36.5\\" hips. I ordered the medium and it's a little loose, but not too bad. I think the size small would've been a better fit through the torso, but it most likely would've been way too short. The only negative I have with this costume is the boot covers. I wear a size 10 shoe, and there's NO WAY it will go over the toes. If your shoe size is a size 5-8, then I'm sure it will be perfect for you. I've decided to wear a pair of black biker boots I've had for years, instead.

The fabric of the dress is like a vinyl coated fabric. That's the only way I can describe it. It has a little stretch to it, too. It's well made and has even stitching throughout. The dress has a zipper up the back... no cheap and gaping Velcro! The bat emblem is an embroidered patch and looks nice. It's sewn evenly across the chest, too. The cape is detachable, with two decent patches of Velcro to keep it on. The mask is a sturdier piece of plastic than I was expecting, and has your standard thin piece of elastic, closed with a small piece of Velcro. I'll probably have to secure it with bobby pins, but other than that it's great. The belt is a hard, yet flexible plastic in the front and on the sides, and it has two yellow fabric strips to tie in the back. I actually like this, as it allows me the option of wearing it at the most flattering spot between my waist and hips. No one will see the tie in the back when you're wearing the cape. The gauntlets (arm pieces) are well made. They've got a little bit of stretch in them. I plan on placing a piece of double sided swim tape up towards the elbow to keep them from scrunching down.

So, all in all, this was a great costume for it's price. Just be careful which vendor you pick. product_title: Columbia Men's 1 1/2 in. Leather Belt With Overlay
review_body:
UPDATE:
After giving it an extensive road test, I don't recommend this belt at all. I'm subtracting one star, giving it 2/5.
The belt is terribly deformed and the most frequently used holes are stretched and ripped. Not 100% leather, it's cardboard or something inside.
-----

It's a nice looking belt. The quality is questionable. It almost seems like some kind of card-stock backing and then leather glued to the face. I really hope that's not the case, but I guess time will tell. It's a very stiff belt, almost folds rather than curls. I haven't had a new belt in quite a long time so I hope I'm just too accustomed to my well broken in leather belt. This one says 100% genuine leather... We'll see.

As for sizing, people should be using common sense. It's a belt, not a pair of shoes. If you're a 38 waist, order at least a 40+ belt. The size of the belt is the last (largest) hole. If you don't want to have to wear it on the largest hole, order something a little larger. (This seems obvious to me... I'm not sure why so many people have problems; on every belt here on Amazon there are sizing complaints, it's a mystery.)

product_title: Trafalgar Men's Cortina Slimfold Wallet
review_headline: Smelled pretty bad, and "Slimfold" isn't a very accurate name
review_body:
This wallet is simple and sturdy - exactly what I was looking for. I didn't want something packed full of excessive pockets, plastic inserts, or any flashy logos, grommets, embroidery - I just wanted a classic leather wallet that could stand up to years of daily use.

There are four card slots on each side, with a sleeve behind each. Each slot is pretty tight, and the bill pocket isn't exactly roomy, so it forces you to keep junk out of your wallet (receipts, expired or unused membership cards, old gift-cards with a couple bucks left on them, etc)

All in all, a solid wallet.

Unfortunately, it's also got some design and (possibly) manufacturing issues that I'm not too thrilled with.

When it first arrived, I noticed that the leather smelled bad - like it had been rubbed down with fish oil or stored in a cannery. It smelled like leather, but the 'fishy' smell was right behind it.

I've had it for a few weeks, and the smell is either fading, or I'm getting used to it. I'm not sure whether it was the source, the storage, or the manufacturing process, but at some point that leather got a good dose of stink.

The "slimfold" name is a bit misleading, as well. Because of the design and the way the card slots are positioned, the wallet is pretty fat when full.

It's close to an inch deep, with 8 cards and a half dozen bills inside. Not HUGE, but definitely not slim.

I may have gotten a bad batch of leather, I haven't seen any other reviews mentioning the smell, but there's a star off for that.

If yours doesn't smell awful, then it's a solid 4-star wallet.

product_title: Cotton Maternity Nursing Undershirts for Breastfeeding Moms - White
review_headline: Great idea, but hard to find a shirt and bra combo that doesn't show holes.
review_body:
I love the idea of this shirt. I nursed my daughter for a year and am now nursing my son. With my daughter I could go to the car or find a dressing room to nurse her. With two kids I use a cover and just stop wherever. In Target once I had to just find a quiet bench in the shoe section and give my daughter some books to occupy herself. I could care less about nursing in public with a cover, but I hate the draft you feel when you know your back fat it hanging out. Not cool! But, I have some Glamourmom tops, and sometimes I just don't like the feeling they have of basically smooshing you like a sports bra. The band can be tight too, and sometimes I just want a real bra. I have the post-pregnancy belly where its obvious I haven't lost the weight I gained. So, its a lot more attractive to have the support of a real nursing bra as opposed to a nursing tank which smooshes them to flatter than the above mentioned belly....I'm having middle school gym locker room flashbacks. Any-who...I thought it would be great to have this top to go over my nice nursing bras.

It's a good idea, but even if your bra perfectly matches the color you can still see the rings from the holes through your top. Its like the reverse of seeing nursing pads through your shirt. I think the best solution I found was to wear the top UNDER by bra. But, you have to wear a bra that perfectly matches or else the bra stands out. So, white bra with with tank not nude bra with white or black tank.

Better than nothing, but so far I like a nursing top or tank better for coverage. I'm getting a bellysock in the mail soon...so if I get a chance I'll come back and update the review if that's a better solution.

review_body:
Pros:

Very heavy duty utility suspenders

well built, reputable brand, strong elastic bands

Cons:

Someone else said on review he received 46in. mine are 52in but I have ordered mine from Bass Pro, and they were all one size too.
I like to review stuff on Amazon to help others make a choice.

I still would give it 5-star rating because this is a quality product.

product_title: Dickies Women's Scoop Neck Tee
review_body:
First, though I wouldn't recommend purchasing this, if you do, be warned that the t-shirts run large for the size chart. I ordered what seemed like a larger size than usual based on their size chart only to find that the shirt was way too big.

The scoop is also too scooped for my tastes.

Still, these aren't the reasons why I'm giving it one star. It gets one star because of two things: The fabric is not soft. I have other tees, and next to them, this is very scratchy. The \\"slubs,\\" which are sort of horizontal ribs, are not soft at all despite being cotton. I've washed it, used fabric softener, etc., and it's still not soft. The difference is very noticeable.

Finally, the rolling of the material on the shoulders isn't done in a way that makes sense. It's only sewn--tacked-- at the top and underneath, so that means when you wash it, the rest of it rolls various ways rather than stays uniformly rolled. Remedying this would probably mean lots of work with an iron and then sewing it all the way around yourself. Not worth it.

In short, the look and feel of the t-shirt are really poor. Not recommended.

product_title: Jockey Sport Boxer Brief 2-Pack Underwear
review_headline: too much spandex, a weird fly and they ride up
review_body: I purchased these underwear hoping they might be similar to the boxer-brief Champions I love but are no longer made.  What I loved about the old Champions is that they were very comfortable, had a fly, didn't ride up, were reasonably priced and worked equally well for high activity or for every day use.      These Jockeys are not a match for those Champions, but I guess they are ok, but I still find myself looking for a pair of something else with more cotton if I'm going to wear them all day.    Pros:    The Jockeys do have a fly, so at least you're spared the embarrassment of having to open the whole front of your pants to take a wee.  I simply don't understand mens' underwear that doesn't have an opening in front.  The Jockeys fly design is weird though, it doesn't open from the side like every other piece of underwear you've probably worn.  It opens horizontally across the front.  I guess it works ok, but certainly no better than side-opening underwear.  Jockeys says its supposed to keep things from getting bunched or some such thing, but its frankly not the easiest opening to use (especially with the amount of spandex and therefore the stretchiness of these underwear, but more on that later).     The Jockey's fit reasonably well.  I'm 5 foot 9 inches and about 160 pounds and the medium size seems like they were designed for people around my size/proportions.  Some other bands I've worn (Hanes) feel like they were designed for much taller people (i.e. if the underwear is sitting comfortably at the waist, there is extra sagging material below the crotch which can bunch and cause chaffing, so either you endure the bunching, or you yank them up to your navel to get the crotch to sit right).  No problems with extra material on these though.    Cons:    The Jockeys have too much spandex and not enough cotton.  I want my boxer-briefs to hug my body, but these maybe go a little too far.  Perhaps they will loosen up over time and after going through the wash, but as ofnow, they fit a little more like bicycle shorts than like underwear.  If you enjoy that degree of constriction in your underwear though, you'll probably love these.  I think the amount of spandex (20%) also contributes to these underwear retaining body heat more than they should.  Jockey says they are supposed to wick moisture, and they do, but I think a little less synthetic fiber would make them less insulating and they wouldn't need to wick moisture so much.  Inevitably, no matter the weather, these underwear end up getting sweaty on me, even if I'm not doing anything aerobic.  Even wearing a simple pair of jeans over them, you'll probably end up with sweaty shorts, which can be uncomfortable.    The Jockeys sit a little low at the hips.  My preference is for underwear that sits right at the hips, these fall a little below the hips.  If you're accustomed to underwear that sits that low, you'll like these, especially if your pants also fall below the hips too.      The Jockeys end up riding up and you'll have to make a trip to the restroom at some point during the day to get everything readjusted.  With boxer briefs, this is almost a given, but I still feel less spandex and more cotton would lessen the problem.      The Jockeys tag in the back of the waist band is a little scratchy.  Jockey should have sewed the edges of the tag under itself so there are no hard edges, or gone without the tag and printed the washing instructions onto the material itself, or moved the tag to the outside of the underwear, or somewhere where it would be less irritating.      Conclusion    I think I'll end up wearing these mostly for my time at the gym, but I doubt they'll make it into the everyday routine.  They aren't comfortable enough to wear all day for me.  They aren't really comfortable enough to sleep in.  They work adequately for some support and moisture wicking, so the gym is probably their best place.

product_title: InCharacter Costumes Women's Maid Marian Costume
review_body:
Have not yet worn this for Halloween, but after trying it on I still think I can give it an accurate review. First, a little background so you know about why I chose this dress out of the many possibilities. My purposes for this was for an Arthurian Legends themed Halloween party, and I was planning on going as the Lady of Shalott. I picked this dress because it was one of the lighter colored ones out there, and it had the three designs that I was going for: pointed inner sleeves, flaring outer sleeves, and a sash (these are designs I've noticed in Shalott artwork). Also, it was relatively cheap; only a little over thirty bucks, even though the original price stated over sixty.

And now for the breakdown.

Pros:

Looks gorgeous, even though I only have an OK figure. It also seemed somewhat warm, but I cannot confirm that as getting the dress on was a bit of a workout. But with the sleeves and clear-to-the-floor skirt, I don't think you need to worry about shivering in an indoor party. But even with all the cons, this really is a GORGEOUS dress. If all you need is to look good for a night, you're covered.

Fit was OK. I got size large, and when it says large it actually means it, unlike most costumes out there. Instead of pushing the boundaries of the size, it was actually slightly TOO large, which is how a large SHOULD be on me.

Cons (unfortunately a bit of these):

That reviewer who stated it sheds? Not kidding. All I did was put it ON and everything around me was glittering with little bits of fuzz that fell off. I could see it on the cover of my black laptop. I'd be almost afraid to launder it, for fear of washing it all off. VERY CHEAP FABRIC. Despite being a velvet of sorts, it is very very thin and will not stand up to much wear and tear.

You need a spotter to get in and out of this thing. There is NO zipper. You have to pull it on and off over your head, and I had to have my sister yank it down so I could get my arms in those sleeves.

Comes crushed. Be prepared to brow-beat the shape back into that headpiece, and iron what you don't want to look wrinkled. This isn't actually that much, as the crushed velvet look is OK with looking, well, crushed. But the veil and that pattern on the front needed straightening.

Really wide neck. Recommend those bras with no straps, because they may show otherwise.

Poorly sewn together. Just from putting it on, I broke free one of the elastic straps that hold the sleeve to your finger. It just snapped loose. Also, several parts of the dress look like they're already bursting seams, probably because they were just missed. Sash is slightly off-center too, so I have to keep twisting the dress.

Headpiece will not stay on head without outside help. Its way to small to fit over any head older than eight. It doesn't look BAD, but it requires work. I just hope I can manage it on a WIG because my real hair is too short for this look.

Summary:

Nice for one night, but don't expect the dress to last. Do NOT pay full price; I've gotten better quality from Wal-Mart costumes. Things to keep in mind would be the wide neckline, possible help with getting in and out of it, finding some way to keep the headpiece on, and don't fluff the dress near food (unless you don't mind eating cheap velvet). It really is too bad it has to have so many cons, because this is a beautiful costume. review_headline: You get what you pay for.
review_body: This hat pin was pretty much everything it claimed to be, a cheap hat pin with CSA on it. All I can say is you get what you pay for. The quality is just a cast mold, nor sure this is even bronze or brass, more like gold colored pot metal. Like other reviews my main complaint was the tacks on the back. They look to be soldered on rather than molded with the rest of the pin, so as soon as you unfold them to attach the pin to your hat they instantly break off at the solder points. So basically the pin becomes unusable to moment you try to use it. If you want to go to the trouble of re-soldering the pins back on or figuring out another way to attach it to your hat then it might be useful, but for me it was just a waste of money. This is one of those cases of a good seller but a bad product.

review_headline: HORRIFIC customer service at this company...
review_body:
I ordered this costume from Spookshop 3 weeks before Halloween in 2013. When it arrived, I took it out of the package, didn't like and put it back in exactly as I had received it, wrapped perfectly in the tissue paper. I sent it back the next day and waited. Then I sent 3 emails to the customer service center which were never returned. Then over the course of the next 3 months, I called FIVE times and each time was told something different by an employee there - "We can't find it" or "I'm not the right person who call help you", "I need to speak to a manager and we'll call you back," (never hearing back) etc. I FINALLY got a hold of someone in late December who informed me that they charge a "restocking" fee and I'd only be receiving less than half the cost of the costume back. NOWHERE did it say they had such a return policy and it sure wasn't in the package I received.

They have HORRIFIC customer service and I would never recommend buying anything from them, especially if you have to make a return! You've been warned!!

I'm a super picky bathrobe person. I wear one every day while I get coffee, so they need to be incredible for me to notice. I have 5 or so bathrobes, and this one has been my go-to robe since I purchased it.

This robe is fantastic:
- Super soft and luxurious feel. The fleece is really, really, plush. A++
- Size is bigger than most bathrobes. Big as in awesome. It comes down to my ankles and right to my hand on the sleeve. Look at the sizing instructions carefully and measure first!
- It looks nicer in person than it does in the pictures. That's rare.

I would purchase this robe again in a heartbeat.

product_title: Capezio Women's Camisole Leotard With Adjustable Straps
review_body:
I love, love, love this leotard. I've bought it in Royal Blue and it looks amazing! Everyone in the class is asking where I've got it, since the color is so great. The other thing is that I absolutely love the material. This is not a cotton leotard, it's completely synthetic, so it dries very very fast. I've never seen any wet spots on it, and after 6 month of wearing and washing, it holds up amazingly. It really looks like new. I wish they would have it in light blue :( Amazon sells another model of the same leotard just in cotton mix material. I've ordered light blue by mistake (I thought that's exactly the same model as I've previously purchased in Royal), and was very disappointed. The fitting is totally different than in this one, fabric and material will wears out pretty fast. So I'll definitely order this one in more colors.

Fitting:
I'm 130 lb 5.8-5.9 ft tall. I ordered Large and it fits perfectly. I could definitely fit in Medium, however I like not to feel the leotard at all when I'm dancing. With Large that's the case and at the same time it stays in place.
Great product! Capezio and Amazon, please please have more of these in nice colors!

product_title: Alpha Industries Men's N-3B Parka Coat
review_body:
I hate to be cold and I have several cold weather coats for varied levels of cold. I bought this to be my #2 cold weather coat. For the coldest weather I have a Canada goose parka that's too warm for anything but sitting still. That coat has generous pockets and everything is workable with gloves on. It's very well thought out.
This alpha parka is very similar in style, but the ergonomics are true to its 1950's origins. The acrylic wrist cuffs are recessed and are EXCELLENT. The pockets are small and snap shut - no velcro. The snaps are difficult to operate with gloves. The outer nylon shell is excellent quality material and is waterproof. The Canada goose is cotton/poly and does get wet in rain. The hood is well lined and is high quality. The fur ruff is synthetic, but looks OK. I'm not a big hood person and prefer a nice warm cap. The pockets are not well insulated - they are outside the insulating layer of the body. The pockets are not large enough for gloves and a hat when you take the coat off to go inside. the 2 way zipper is YKK and works well, but I wish it was brass for this price.
The body is insulated fairly well with poly insulation, but I haven't worn it yet in real cold weather. The sleeve insulation is very good. It is very wind resistant. the draw cords do not have "locks" on them like so many other coats have. You actually have to tie a knot, and that's tough with gloves in the cold.
I have a recently made, real N3-B with a 100% cotton shell from a military contractor (DJ Manufacturing) and this coat compares well with the real McCoy. The only difference is the nylon vs cotton shell and metal zippers. leather reinforcements at pockets and drawstrings are nice. The inside lining is smooth and has horizontal stitching to keep the insulation in place. the inside pocket is shallow and very basic - no flap and no zipper/snap. I think it's very well made and I checked the button stitching and it appears good. Others commented on poor button attachment.

This Alpha parka is much better than the Knox Armory version (also sold by Alpha). I bought one of those and returned it due to a noticeable decrease in the quantity of insulation. If you want a well made N3-B, I think this is the best pick short of a used Military issue N3-B.

product_title: Agave Men's Gringo Classic Fit Grey Jean
review_body:
I have known about Agave for some time now as I have been buying their shirts and sweaters for many years. Everything about their clothing is top notch however, with that being said, I never purchased their jeans as I just wasn't a big fan of their styles, a little bit too straight and narrow for my taste. It was almost as if they were aiming more for adults that wanted a very plain and simple style of jean and I prefer my jeans to be slightly distressed so they dont look brand spanking new when you get them. Don't get me wrong, I am not a fan of extreme distressing where there are holes and the jeans look like they have been worn for 10 years. Just subtle distressing to take that brand new look out of the jeans.

Well thankfully Agave has really updated their styles and brought them more in line with the current trends and in particular, the styles I look for with my jeans. I used to go through their entire line and not find a single pair that interested me. Now its pretty much the other way around and there are so many pairs I am interested in that I have trouble choosing which ones to buy. I cant buy them all because unfortunately Agave jeans aren't cheap. In fact, nothing Agave sells is cheap and that is really the only negative thing about Agave, their clothing is a bit pricey but I for one think its absolutely worth it.

First their jeans are made of top quality Supima cotton. In case your unaware Supima Cotton is 100% USA grown Pima cotton. The name \\"Supima\\" is really an abbreviation for Superior Pima. Pima cotton is a generic name for extra-long staple (ELS) cotton and to make a long story short Pima cotton is softer and stronger than regular cotton which makes it more comfortable and more durable. Trust me, you can feel the difference the second you touch a Supima piece of clothing. They feel like butter.

Second Agave use old school machines like Shuttle Looms to make their jeans. They are far less efficient than some of the newer machines being used today but there is a reason the top jean makers in the world use such machines, because the craftsmanship is significantly higher in quality and that is what a quality pair of jeans is all about. Agave understand this and pride themselves on such principals.

Last but not least everything they make, jeans included, are made in the USA. Yes that's right, that isn't a typo. They are made in the good ol USA, California to be precise. I am so sick of seeing the words Made in China or Made in Taiwan. I try to buy as many made in the USA products as I can and it isn't easy. A lot of times you have to buy China products as the US equivalent simply doesn't exist. Its disgusting. Well thankfully there are companies out there like Agave that at least give people a choice in regards to certain products. I am proud to support such a company and I am proud to wear their clothing.

As for this particular pair of jeans, they are outstanding. I love all the different colored jeans that Agave now offers. Grey, Black, Olive, White, Brown, Indigo, Ect.. Grey is one of my favorite colors in regards to jeans and this is one of the nicest pairs I have seen yet. Like all Agave jeans they are as soft as butter. You simply have to feel a pair to understand just how soft a pair of jeans can be. As I explained earlier in this review, I prefer my jeans to have very subtle distressing and this pair of jeans is a perfect example of just what I look for in this regard. They are absolutely perfect. Light sanding on the thighs, light sanding and a tiny bit of fraying on the bottom leg seams. Absolutely perfect.

The only negative thing I can say about these jeans is in regards to the sizing and this is a problem I have with all of their jeans. I need a 30\\" to 31\\" inseam size and unfortunately the vast majority of Agave jeans only come in one inseam size, 35\\". So I have to take each pair and have them professionally altered to 30\\" or 31\\" which adds an additional 15 bucks to each pair. I would love to see Agave start offering different inseam sizes.

Bottom line - There are so many companies out there making jeans that it can literally make your head spin. Well if your looking for high quality jeans that are made in the USA then Agave is the top choice in my book. Yes they are pricey but its pretty easy finding them on sale and its without a doubt 100% worth the price. You will never find a softer, more comfortable pair of jeans, period.

Highly, and I do mean Highly, recommended!

product_title: Slimmy Redux 1 Pocket Wallet - 68mm (X1S1)
review_body:
I carried a pretty standard Kenneth Cole bi-fold wallet for years and loved it. I've tried a fancy (read: weird) rubber wallet, a \\"smart\\" money clip that held cash and cards, as well as simply carrying folded cash in my pocket. I really like the idea of streamlining what I carry but every time I've tried a different wallet I've always gone back to my bi-fold.

I saw the Slim Slimmy somewhere or another and decided to give a try, and I'm glad I did. I've had the wallet for several months now and overall I've pleased with it. The wallet is very well put together, quality stitching, and very nice leather (has that great leather smell).

As even the manufacturer points out this isn't a magic \\"shrink your back breaker wallet\\" gimmick. It forces you to minimize what you carry by only accommodating a small amount of cargo. It'll carry a decent amount of currency, a few plastic cards, and a few business cards. Personally I carry about three bills, two plastic cards (ID and debit card), and two paper cards. Everything else I leave in my car.

This setup works well for me, but it's worth mentioning that adding too much to the wallet can cause items to fall out so if you're a heavy cash user, you have tons of IDs/credit cards, etc. you may want to try another wallet.

review_body: * color: The white and blue is awesome looking. I managed to keep the white white so far, but it does get dirty if you start rubbing against cars. The good thing is it's waterproof so the stains come off under the snow.    * sizing:  It's true to size. I'm 5'2\\", 105-110lbs, bought an S and I have margin in the jacket.    * warmth: I'm the type of girl who complains it's freezing when it's 50 degrees Fahrenheit, and I was actually warm in this jacket with just a long sleeve thermal underneath, skiing in a  windy snow storm. I used to wear a tank top, a long-sleeve thermal, a long sleeve shirt, a wool sweater, and a fleece under my old insulated Columbia convert jacket, just to tell you how much warmth I usually need. So yeah, this jacket is WARM!    * 2 long arm vents at arm pits    * tuck-away ski skirt. It's not in the way if you don't want to use it    * pockets: tons of them.    + inner shell has 2 \\"bottom\\" outer pockets (you know where you expect them to be on a jacket) with zippers    + outer shell has 2 inner pockets at the chest level: one mesh no-zip goggle pocket and one zip mp3 player pocket with a small hoop to hold your headset.    + outer shell has 2 \\"bottom\\" outer pockets with zippers   pockets complaints (minor)    + NO pocket at the end of the sleeve (near your hand) to put a scannable pass.     + Zippers are closed when in upwards position so if you attach your gloves to the zippers it will pull it open.    pockets notes:     + If you have electronics and plan to put them in the bottom pockets, I would put them in the pockets of the inner jacket. Even though the outer shell is very waterproof, I found my cell phone to be a little damp when left in the outer pocket of the outer shell in very stormy conditions (it was fine in normal conditions). That's probably because you don't get the full effect of the waterproofness if you're using only half of the outer shell to protect it. Also, if you put it in the inner shell, it would be within the snow skirtif you use it. I don't know about the inner chest mp3 player pocket because I haven't tried it.     * attaching your pass:  As said above, no sleeve pocket for the newer scannable passes, and no hook to attach the older metal hook + sticker passes. That's probably my main complaint about this jacket.

product_title: Reel F/X Third Eye Prosthetics
review_body: I ordered this piece for a LARP costume.  Out of the box, there are a few small details that need to be addressed before utilizing the prosthetic to its full potential.      First off, there is WAY too much extra latex \\"skin\\" around the eye.  Unless you have a massive forehead, there is no reason for it.  Very sharp scissors can be used to trim down this excess latex, leaving about 3/4th inch radius of the skin around the eye lid area should suffice and leave enough area for your spirit gum to bond.      The only other issue is while the prosthetic itself is beautiful, the stock paint job on the eyeball is butt ugly.  Get yourself some basic modeling paint (Games Workshop, P3, Vallejo, etc) and repaint the entire thing.  If you want it to look REALLY awesome, after you're done painting (and it has dried) apply a layer of gloss varnish to the eyeball area.  Once it dries, it'll look like a real, moist eye.      Other than, you'll just have to use a combination of normal and costume makeup to match the skin tone to your own.      In anycase, this is still an awesome prosthetic for Halloween or LARPing.  I'd suggest it to anyone.

product_title: The Mountain Three Wolf Moon Short Sleeve Tee
review_body: Whoever said, `more than two wolves are wasted' is obviously a fat idiot.  Every wolf on this shirt is ABSOLUTELY necessary, which is why I spelled `absolutely' with ten capital letters, and would have spelled it with eleven capital letters if `absolutely' was spelled that way.  The same goes for if it was spelled with twelve letters.  So on and so forth.    Each wolf howls for a different reason, but all three reasons link back to an ancient yearning that never has, and never will be satisfied. This yearning is mine as well.  It's a three wolf moon shirt when it sits in my closet--it becomes a four wolf moon shirt when I put it on.    Of course any responsible review of this shirt must pay homage to the role of the moon, whose story is forever old and forever true.  The patience and wisdom of the moon has never been captured before--until now.  Some truths are best captured through song, some best captured through dance, and some best captured on a cotton t-shirt made in the US and assembled in Mexico.    I've worn this shirt for the past five moons and have begun to wonder--am I wearing the shirt, or is it wearing me?  After another few months, I'm sure I'll discover the answer, and by then, I'll be ready to embrace the truth.

product_title: L'ovedbaby Long-Sleeve Overall
review_body: I loved the L'ovedbaby nursing shawl, so I was excited to find out they make clothes too, but... I'm so disappointed at the apparent lack of quality for a small, higher-priced brand! When we received ours there was one snap that seemed not-so-snappy. After two wears that snap would not stay closed, and after five or six the leg area was hopeless. More of the snaps started failing and we just couldn't use it anymore.    The snaps do not have any markings on them like some others (it seems there are brand name snaps) and the only conclusion I can reach is that these are just cheap.    Unfortunately I was not able to return our suit, but I recommend you do not buy this unless you promise yourself you'll check for bad snaps and go through the return hassle if they are defective. It IS cute and soft and simple, and I would have given it five stars if the snaps worked! It sounds like some people are lucky and get good snaps, but believe the bad reviews too! There are similar bad reviews on some of the other L'ovedbaby clothes items.    BTW, we got the blue and it is not as bright as this picture. It's more like traditional hospital scrubs color. IF you order, I also recommend going a size up from what you expect your baby's size to be, although the fabric does stretch out a little through a day of wear.

product_title: Double-Stick No Iron No Sew Fashion Hem Tape for Denim (Jeans, Pants, Skirt, Short)
review_body:
In my experience all these hem tapes work on the same basic premise, i.e. temporarily altering the length of pants by using what is essentially 2 sided scotch tape to create a temporary hem. The differences I have found are in the size/dimensions of each precut strip, how well the stick in place, and finally how much residue do they leave behind after being removed.

THis particular product has smaller cut strips which means that more of them are needed. I could live with that but the adhesive on them was not enough to hold my jeans hem in place at all.. even when i used four per leg. I have used another brand where the strips were over 6 inches long and I had to cut them to my desired length.. it was a pain in the you know what, but when i put them in they stayed that way and lasted the whole day. I bought these because i thought it would be easier not having to cut them down, but in the process sacrificed the quality of the product.

product_title: Carhartt Men's Big & Tall Heavyweight Cotton Thermal Crewneck Top
review_headline: Made in El Salvador. Stitching separating after 5 weeks
review_body:
I had high expectations for this thermal shirt and felt it was going to be worth paying a premium to get Carhartt quality. This shirt is a bit thicker and more comfortable than some other thermal shirts. Looked ok as well and did well keeping me warm in cold weather the few times I wore it.

Today after the 4th wash (warm water wash and tumble dry on low) I saw the stitching separating from the collar down the top of the shoulder (about an inch is already separated along the seam and its now a hole. I wasnt wearing this but about once per week on the weekend and didn't even subject it to any real work.

Well its not made in the USA but in El Salvador. Just another cheaply made import and if I had known it was not US made I would have passed on it (never would have thought Carhartt would move production out of the USA). Way to pricey for a cheaply made import. I am a week out of the Amazon return period so I guess I am stuck with it. Will contact Carhartt to see how they stand behind the shirt and update the review if things change. I miss American made products.

3/6/13 - update: I contacted Carhartt and they gave me an RMA # and I have sent it back. They got the shirt on 2/27/13 so they have had it a week. I called today to see what was going on and they said they have to examine the shirt which will take them till around 3/19/13 (about 3 weeks to examine it) and then they will either return it back to me or replace it. Of course by the time I get anything back winter will be about over. Good efficient customer service goes a long way with me. How it takes more than a day or two to inspect the shirt is beyond me. Anyway maybe they have to send it out to some lab and have fabric engineers examine the seam to determine what has caused the failure.

product_title: The Mountain Three Wolf Moon Short Sleeve Tee
review_body: I was a skeptic when it came to the mythic powers of this tee shirt until I witnessed them for myself. I was at the Woodstock Fair, a local agricultural exposition, satisfying my annual craving for irony. Between the steady diet of deep-fried Twinkies and giant pickles on sticks and the two-hour late performance of Dennis DeYoung, former lead singer of Styx, I had reached and exceeded my irony quota. I decided to take a stroll through the midway to bask in the neon and flourescent glow of the Scrambler and Giant Slide when I saw her, a vision of thrift store loveliness clad in too-tight jeans and a black rhinestone-encrusted tee proclaiming her a 'clASSy Bitch.' She looked at me from under her feathered bangs with a black-mascaraed sneer that told me that I would never, ever see what was frolicking so joyously under her tee. I turned to the nearest vendor and saw it. The Three Wolf Moon shirt. I purchased it, put it on and ran off in search of my carny queen. When I got close to her, it was as if she sensed my presence, or perhaps the power of the shirt. She turned, took the lit Marlboro from her mouth, and exhaled the smoke slowly as she surveyed the new addition to my wardrobe. \\"Damn,\\" she said, in that low, smoky voice of hers, \\"that is a fine looking three wolf moon shirt. Follow me.\\" With that she turned into one of the darker alcoves of the midway, on the way back to the trailers these itinerant merchants call home. There, behind the Bump-O-Rama, in the light of the Zipper, we consummated our mutual lusts, I for her, and she for my Three Wolf Moon shirt. She took the shirt with her, and I never saw Tawny Sue again, but I will always have the memory of the magical powers over a certain class of women possessed by this magical garment. The only suggestion that I have for any future purchaser of this shirt, is to use protection. review_headline: Quality Exceeds Expectations - Built to Last
review_body:
I was looking for a better western quality belt with a simple design; nothing too fancy or decorative. Some belts I've purchased recently started to lose their shape and show signs of wear much sooner than expected. On those belts, the leather was not top quality and a bit thin. This belt, on the other hand, is constructed of thick leather with beautifully finished stitching and edges. I've only had it a few days, but based on the build quality, I expect it to last a long time. Whoever manufactured the belt probably also makes western saddles, from the look of it.

One other note: the buckle is a simple design, held on by screws. It goes with the rest of the design. But many cowboy types are going to replace that buckle with another of their choosing anyway and the screws make it simple to swap.

I am very satisfied with my purchase. The quality exceeded my expectations.

product_title: SPF® Adult Long Sleeve T-Shirt
review_body: Dermatologists tell us that the single greatest cause of aging and damaged skin is exposure to the sun, with 2 million new cases of skin cancer reported yearly.  We might use sun screen on our face and hands, but often the arms and torso are left unprotected imagining that our clothing is already blocking any damaging rays. But a light colored t-shirt is said to have less than a 7 UPF rating and less if it becomes wet.  After noticing sun damage on my arms, especially living in the southeast, it seemed like a good idea to take a few more precautions, so I searched for some shirts designed to offer much greater protection and found these on Amazon.  There are several companies that make this type of clothing, mostly at much greater cost.  But they all seemed to be made from synthetic fabric which I prefer to avoid in favor of pure cotton which I find more comfortable, has great wicking properties to evaporate persperation and is a renewable and natural resource.  It's difficult to order any clothing item sight unseen with a strong possibility the fit is wrong and drape is awkward,  Amazon has such incredible customer service that I decided to give it a try and ordered one in black.  It was delivered promptly and to my relief the fit was perfect.  The proportions are generous without being big or oversized.  The fabric is preshrunk and so far I haven't noticed any change in it's size after washing.  The cotton is soft and there's no indication that it has any treatment or anything to distinguish it from any other shirt.  The price was reasonable especially compared to other competitors' products. It seems well constructed and I expect it to be durable.  The only thing that could be improved on is that it wasn't an Amazon Prime item and so shipping was an extra expense, though not unreasonable. In short I'm very happy with the purchase and plan to order more.

product_title: Travelon Set Of 2 Luggage Tags
review_headline: Lots of pros & only one con
review_body:
I am loving these. Here's why:

* BRIGHT colors. We bought 2 pink sets and 2 green sets for our new (teal blue) luggage and you really cannot help but see them on the luggage. I imagine on a darker background they would stand out even more--a definite plus when you are competing with 100+ people who are all lunging toward the same black, beat-to-all-heck suitcases on the conveyor belt.

* Hard plastic shell. I've had the leather tags, gel-type flexible tags, and now I am obsessed with these hard shelled tags. The area where the strap meets the tag on the leather tags gets bent up and weakens relatively quickly. The gel tags just look cheap to me, and all sorts of dirt and crud gets stuck in them. These look pretty slick if you don't pay attention to my cr@ppy handwritten name in the window.

* Easy (yet not TOO easy) to open to change name & contact info. You need to remove the little "belt" that loops through the tag and then swivel the cover piece to access the laminated identification sticker. The rubber belt is pretty strong--I'm not always the sharpest tool in the shed and attempted to simply pull the belt apart with my super-strong mom fingers. After several futile attempts, I checked out the construction and realized that the little belt holes and pegs were on the underside of the belt. In other words, unless a thief uses scissors or nail clippers, it is highly unlikely that anyone would have the time and know-how to quickly and surreptitiously remove the tag from my luggage.

Only one con that I can think of: The identification plate that comes in the tag can't be removed to use in a printer for clearer name/contact info. If you really want to use a printed/typed label, you'll need to measure the label & location of the window, then print it and cut it to size. I am waaaay too lazy for that kind of business. However, if your handwriting is particularly poor or you want a more professional look, this is definitely an option. In fact, you can take it even further and buy some contact paper, cut it to size, and cover your home-printed label to make it even more durable and attractive.ly an option. review_headline: Good value and good fit ... made better with the addition of a hook and button closure.
review_body: I have purchased these Docker D3's for years and have enjoyed their comfort, styling and value above all.  Another benefit to me, personally, is the fact that they are one of very, very few dress slacks being offered in my size (32 x 34).  With the latest updates, the D3's now have a hook closure (in addition to a button on the inner side of the waistband), rather a center button only as on the previous design.  I see this as a value-add feature that could prove useful should the threads holding the button ever break or unravel over time.  Per Murphy's Law, this would naturally occur at work, at a wedding, a funeral ... or some other equally inconvenient moment.  I feel that the hook could be a nice back-up in that instance.  Additionally, the hook and button when used together probably help reduce the stress on each other.  Overall, I have been happy with the durability of the pants as a whole ... although after a year of nearly daily wear and weekly laundering, the material does gradually lose it's shape and sharpness. I am 5'6\\" and medium weight so am not exceptionally tall. I would be so embarrassed if one of my grandchildren would see me wearing these, I would probably be gently led to the nearest retirement home. They are fairly light weight so will be better for summer wear.  I do take responsibility for my purchase, the model wearing them is also too tall for the pant. product_title: Maternity - Most Popular Funny Maternity Dark T-Shirt by CafePress
review_headline: Not a maternity shirt, but it is a decent T-shirt with a cute print
review_body:
Original (2/15/11) - The image on Amazon is of a shirt on which the sides have been pinched behind it. This gives the illusion that the shirt is a maternity shirt - in reality, it is just a regular sized T-shirt. Also, image appears to have been stretched vertically and squished horizontally - this adds to the visual impression of the image as a maternity shirt. This by itself does not warrant a 1-star - a shirt is a shirt after all and the T-shirt is still wearable and of decent quality. However...

In the image, the hands/feet appears to be pretty low on the shirt - closer to the abdomen area. On the actual shirt I received, the hands/feet was in the upper area of the shirt, putting the print right in the upper chest area and nowhere near the bump where the baby actually is. If it was near the baby bump, it would be kind of cute - but having hands/feet on your breasts is kind of lame. Maybe this was a misprint? I don't know - I also purchased the Peeking Baby maternity shirt from CafePress and had issues with that as well so this appears to be a trend...

The print I received was very faded, almost as if it was rubbed out.

I sent an email complaint to Cafe Press regarding the print location, but as of yet it has been ignored. Should this issue be addressed, I will revisit this review. But if the product I received is representative of the standard, I would not recommend purchasing this at all.

EDIT (2/18/11) - I contacted Cafe Press regarding the faded print and was promptly sent a replacement. The print impression was normal and not faded. The location of the print itself, while still not as low as I would have liked (square on the baby bump), it was at least in the center of the shirt so the print ends up on the upper portion of the baby bump - cute! I was very pleased with Cafe Press' customer service and the speed of their response.

The last few batches Dad and I got kept declining in quality though and I decided to try something new: Dockers.  Overall these are a good pair of briefs. Thick cotton, comfy waistband, good room up front, and they look really clean cut on. One complaint is the tag: the thread has come unbound on several pairs. Another complaint is that as the day goes on the back of them gets loose, creating an extra bag of fabric on the back that looks bad and isn't the most comfortable overnight. I sleep in just briefs so I want to be comfy. I will be ordering another size down if I stick with Dockers next time, I already sized down to a 34" when I wear a 36-38" in jeans. Good support and I like my tighty whities.  UPDATE 3/24 These have gotten baggier and bigger as time has passed. Time to go back to Stafford briefs. They at least keep my package in place and don't ride up like a diaper all day and night. Might try low rise now too.

review_body: It is incredibly difficult to find suits for me as I am a 34S, and this was the only place I found on Amazon that offered a suit this size. I was a little wary of the low price tag, but I really needed a suit so I went ahead and brought this.    I received the suit today -- quality is good, the wool's not the same quality as good Super 140s, but it's not bad either. Fit is better than any 36S I've tried. Pants are cut nicely, could be a little tighter (I hate pleated pants), but the distance between the belt and the crotch is a little too big and so the pants actually sit close to my belly button (bad). All in all, I think I will probably lengthen the sleeves by 1/2 inch, hem the pants, and perhaps tuck in the chest/stomach slightly, which is very reasonable considering it's a mail-order suit.    The suit is on par with a $150-200 suit from Men's Wearhouse. The fit is generally great, the only gripe I have is that the suit was a little dirty out of the box, so I will have to dry clean it before wearing it for the first time. Definitely worth the Benjamin--good for someone's first or second suit, but don't expect too much!

product_title: Organic Maternity Belly Belt for Active Moms-to-Be
review_headline: Cache Coeur brand belly band is excellent, runs small
review_body:
From reading the reviews under this listing, I'm getting the impression that multiple different brands/styles of organic cotton belly band might be sold using the same listing, which is confusing. I hope Amazon sorts this out.

Anyway, my belly band ordered through this listing ended up being a Cache Coeur brand (not Belly Moms brand per the listing description) organic cotton belly band (sold by Moda Angelo and fulfilled by Amazon), so the 5 stars is for that product.

I previously bought a Curad Maternity Belt (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B005MT0MD4) that provides stronger support, but the material unfortunately badly irritates my sensitive skin. I originally bought this cotton belly band to wear under the Curad to prevent skin irritation (which it does nicely), and it turns out the cotton belly band also provides good light/medium support on its own. It doesn't show up under most clothes, and it doesn't have Velcro fasteners to catch on things, unlike the Curad, but it's definitely a lighter-duty support garment. It's comfy enough to wear to sleep, though, and helps to support the belly then, too. It hasn't rolled up on me yet, though it doesn't cover as much of my eighth-month belly as shown in the product photo.

FYI, the band is not 100% cotton (though the cotton portion is stated as organic) - it wouldn't stretch if it was. The Cache Coeur one I received is 83% cotton, 11% polyamide (a sweat-wicking material), and 6% elastane (Spandex), and it hasn't irritated my super sensitive skin, even after wearing it all day.

The band does seem to run small. I typically wear a small to medium in American sizes, but I had to get a large for the belly band. I'm guessing it's because Cache Coeur is a French brand, and European sizes tend to run smaller.

review_headline: The North Face's version of the Canada Goose Antarctic parka
review_body:
The issue parka for the US Antarctic Program is the [[ASIN:B000W01BCO Canada Goose Men's Expedition Parka]] which is quite nice, super warm, and rather expensive. The North Face makes this parka, called the McMurdo after the US Antarctic base, which is intended to be a less expensive version with similar cold weather capability.

I've owned one of these for the last four or five Minnesota winters and have used it just a few times. It's actually too warm most of the time to use this, but for sub-zero ice fishing or the like, this would be the choice. Great coat, but definitely both cheaper and less expensive than the Canada Goose.

This is also available in youth sizes which could be useful.

product_title: Satin Self Tie Bow Tie
review_headline: Pros: It won't fray.  Cons: It's still flimsy
review_body:
What I can say in this tie's favor is that it was smooth and silky, but perhaps too smooth and silky. It felt flimsy and it didn't quite hold its shape in the way I would have liked. Having now tried ties from TheTieBar, Marlon Garci, and PenSee, I now know that there are thicker options out there with better, easier to tie material. Ultimately I wouldn't say that it has the "it" feel that goes into more formal bowties, and I wouldn't recommend this for a true white-tie occasion.

There are some things to take into consideration that I wouldn't consider positives or negatives. For example, it's definitely a smaller tie. The material is a bit shiny. The adjustment also does not have any measurements, but this should not be too much of an issue once you find the length that works for you, or if you already have bow ties that have been adjusted to their proper length that you can compare it to.

product_title: Dorfman Pacific Men's Brushed Twill-and-Mesh Safari Hat with Genuine Leather Trim
review_headline: Just a pinch more might've done it for me.
review_body:
I am glad that I ordered the 3XL, as this hat is still just a bit snug. I own an Akubra hat that is Size 64 in Aussie-measure, equivalent to a Size 8 US. That fits me perfectly, but everything I've read suggests that should more be seen as a 2x than 3. Goes to show you, there's no real equivalence. Buy it, try it, and be prepared to send it back if you have to.

So far, the hat itself has been super. The "genuine leather trim" is the chin cord, and even that appears to be bonded leather. It was way more an inconvenience to me than any help I might ever expect from it, so it's been relegated to a closet shelf somewhere. The hat has a nice wide brim for shade, and a mesh-sided crown to allow plenty of flow-through ventilation. I wanted something that would keep rain off my glasses and sun off my nose and ears, while not causing me to drip sweat like the fur felt hat from Down Under brings about when we're above freezing. I also need to have a very large hat. This meets all those needs, but could've gotten 5 stars from me with another centimeter or so of sweatband perimeter.

product_title: Austria Habsburg Iron Crown Order Medal Orden Award WWI
review_headline: Not one of Oshi Regalia's better repros.
review_body:
The medal itself is OK, but it's a flat square edged repro, unlike the original, which takes the actual 3D form of the bird with softer edges and thicker. I have some of Oshi's other reproductions and I am convinced that they can do better than this!
The engraving in and of the eagle itself is not like the actual original, and the crown underneath is just a chunk of metal, where in the real one it is hollow. The shape of the crown on top of the eagles is also really really off from the original. I know Oshi can do detail work like this easily, but they didn't take that extra step. I don't know what they were thinking when they made this.

You know things aren't good when the ribbon gets a paragraph of its own... The ribbon is very very short, barely enough to go around the neck,and is crudely cut. One end is obviously cut with a normal scissors, and fraying at the end. The other end is fraying a little and is really slanted. They were either in a rush or did not care to give a high quality ribbon along with the expensive medal (twice the price as it is on eBay).

Overall, I am disappointed in this product because I know that Oshi makes some of the best reproductions available.

To give you an idea of what the real one looks like I posted several photos.

review_body:
This are excellent cargo/work shorts. My only minor complaints with them is:

#1) The main front pockets (especially the right side where the knife pad is stitched into it) needs to be cut more straight down the thigh. The way the interior of the pocket is cut it causes teh butt of larger knives to ride stightly forward (ie, the pocket is stitched such that it begins its forward sweep too soon... the pocket should be deeper and straighter on the pinky side (as you put your hand in)). It's hard to explain in words... easy to show in person. :)

#2) the "cell phone" pocket is too shallow for an iPhone (only one of the most popular phones in existence!). So you are really kind of forced to carry it in a different pocket instead.

But neither of these issues was enough to dissuad me from buying two pairs. And I will be buying the pants model of them as well... really excellent garments.

product_title: RedSkyTrader Mens European Knight Jousting Helmet One Size Fits Most Metallic
review_headline: Good, but you get what you pay for
review_body:
This is a very nice looking helmet, made of decent quality steel and sporting a reasonable polish. There are some things you should be aware of, however.

First, the helmet's construction isn't apparent by the picture (if you're on amazon mobile.) The \\"visor\\" does move up, but it isn't just the visor; the entire helmet is basically bifurcated and hinged on top. When you open it, the entire front half of the helmet flips up, making it impossible to wear without straps, which are not included. This problem is compounded by the fact that both halves do not stay flush against each other, which means it wants to stay partially open all the time. I was able to fix this by cutting off the bottom part and making the gorget collar seperately attached to the back of the helm so the visor is independent, but not everyone will have access to the same tools I do.

Second, the pieces of the helmet were obviously cut from sheet steel, and not all the edges were buffed down. There aren't any sharp edges, but definitely some pointy corners that might dig into your temple when trying to get the helmet on. Not a problem if you're wearing chainmail, but there you are.

But hey, its a great looking helmet, and not cheap looking, so for fifty bucks I'm happy. Not a bad choice for the weekend knight.

review_body:
Straw Braid Natural Hat / B001A67NNU

I bought this hat because I wanted a good hat to use outside - something with a wide brim to keep the sun off, with a string tie to keep the hat *on* in the strong wind, and I liked the gentle slope of this hat, which meant that I wouldn't have to worry about the fit against my head, sweaty hair, or feeling too contained.

First off, measurements: I'd say this is about a 17.5\\" diameter, although the description says 17\\", so I could be a little off. I'll also buy their statement of 5\\" deep - that's a bit harder to measure, but sounds about right. This hat is VERY floppy, so I don't know where they are getting their description of \\"stiff\\", but I guess floppy is alright.

The string tie on this is a joke - thin, fraying, and held with a single knot that can't be cinched easily. I'm going to get to a crafts store and get a thick bead and a replacement faux-leather string (so it won't slip and slide through the bead) and create a proper cinch-tie. I *am* pleased that the two holes that the tie slides through are reinforced properly with metal rings.

Overall, this looks and feels a little cheap, but in a functional I-got-what-I-paid-for kind of way, not in a I-was-ripped-off kind of way.

~ Ana Mardoll

product_title: Underworks Mens Microfiber Compression Tank
review_headline: Not the Greatest Compression Shirt, but it's allright...
review_body: I've been shopping around for compression shirts since I've lost nearly 100lbs over the past year and a half, leaving me with some extra saggy skin in bad places (man boobs, love handles, you name it).  I bought this after having purchased another (more expensive) Underworks Compression shirt that worked marvelously.  All in all, it's decent, though I probably won't be buying any more of this particular style.    While the price is nice (only about $25, as opposed to the $40+ I've spent on other similar shirts), it is a double-edged sword.    The Pros...  -Some minor compression does improve your \\"look\\" a little bit.  -Very light and comfortable...  it feels like a regular tank.    The Cons...  -The shirt doesn't have as much compression as other similar shirts, and in fact, feels almost like a \\"man-bra\\"- it seems to do some minor \\"lifting\\" and \\"tucking\\" in problem areas (chest, love handles, etc), but not much else.  Sure, it'll make your \\"man boobs\\" look better, but it won't make 'em look any smaller, as other such shirts will do.  This is a shame, because the other Underworks shirt I own (a more expensive \\"t-shirt\\" style one) almost completely erases problem areas, whereas this one just makes them look a little bit better.  -The material is VERY translucent, and in the right lighting, it practically looks like you aren't even wearing anything, which can be embarrassing if you aren't totally covered up over the shirt.  You need to wear at least one other layer over top of it.  -Another problem is that the size isn't as \\"accurate\\" as my other shirts.  All of my other shirts (compression or regular) are either XL or XXL.  I bought this in XL, because a plain Large is way too small for me in general.  Unfortunately, while the sizing feels pretty much about right on my gut and chest, it's just too darned big in other areas- it can easily stretch down to my lower thighs. (and I do mean \\"easily\\", I'm not forcing it, it just goes down that far as I pull it on)  Because Ialways tuck compression shirts in (they ride up easily), it almost feels like once it goes past my belly, it turns into a skirt inside of my jeans.  Just a bit awkward at first.  If I had to go back, I'd probably buy a size smaller, just because the material is so \\"stretchy.\\"    I can't complain too much.  At almost half the price of other compression shirts, it does a decent job.    But if you're serious about compression, I'd say spend a little extra.      I give it a 3 out of 5.  It's allright.  Not good, not bad.  Just allright.

The design of this gloves is pretty smart, it has flexible back and soft protective material in the palm area. Soft material is very good for light duty work and provides very good \\"feel\\" of items, which exceptionally helpful when picking up small items (driver bits, nails, etc.).

However, as this gloves are targeted for light duty and precision work, it will not last for repetitive heavy abrasion. Seriously, people who complaint about the wear should get another type of gloves. It is simply no solution to offer good feel and high wear resistant at the same time. At least, not for $20.

So I just bought another 2 pairs to keep them around. One in my car and one in my house, they comes in different colors too. It is a bit pricey than other brand, but at the end, you get what you pay for. This things has been so popular and been around for a very long time, you can't go wrong with it.

The good:
- Good fit
- Can pick up small items
- Durable with light duty work

The bad:
- Relatively pricey (can be $3-5 cheaper)

review_headline: These may not last as long as Spanx, but they're many times cheaper. Do the math.
review_body:
My only other compression shirt experience was a Spanx I wore constantly over the course of three months or so. I only bought a single one because it was so expensive ($60) that I couldn't justify buying more. I probably washed it four times a week. Eventually it just kinda came apart, but by that time it had lost a noticeable amount of its tightness. In other words it was about what I expected. It got the job done, it's but just not economical to stock up on them.

On the other hand, this Underworks tank seems almost as good (if not just as good) in terms of compression. I've worn it about five times and washed it twice. One nice thing about having a tank vs. a T is the tank doesn't have armpits that will and make your shirt look and feel gross. Wear an undershirt over this tank, and you'll catch most of the sweat that way. This should allow you to wear the shirt twice or even three times without washing it (unless you secrete rotten egg yolks or something).

Ultimately this shirt will probably not last as long as the Spanx did, but I can buy three of these for the price of that one Spanx. This will give me three shirts to rotate, and the money will go farther this way.

If you're new to compression shirts, $20 may seem steep for an undergarment, but compare this price to what else is out there. :\

product_title: Kenneth Cole New York Men's Vintage Twill Jacket
review_headline: keeps me warm and looking good.
review_body:
I have owned only two Kenneth cole products previously; a pair of sunglasses anda button down shirt. I think I may have to get a few more after my experience with this jacket.

The pictures show a slightly shiny jacket, which is acurrate. It appears black or gray depending on the light, though the shininess is minimal and subtle. It looks excellent in person. The zipper pockets add very nice touches and it has some nice accents in the elbow covers. I have found the Jacket to be quite useful with all it's pockets. It really is very convenient to have so many.

The jacket seems to take some influence from a motorcycle jacket but making the styles subtle and very practical looking. I have received a few compliments on it. It offers an excellent designer look, but remains modest enough that it is appropriate for most any occasion.The style is flexible enough that I wore it to a heavy Metal concert by Meshuggah and the next day wore it out to dinner with my girlfriend.

It should be known this is a jacket and not a coat. though it is very warm down to about 15 degrees, you won't be shoveling the driveway in it. The liner does help and it keeps me warm during this very cold Minnesota winter. It's perfect to wear going out, but for sustained outdoor use in below freezing temperatures, you'll likely need something thicker.

I have found the jacket to be a bit snug fitting. Too much thick clothing underneath can make it tight. It does get better after the break-in period though and permit a moderate hooded sweatshirt underneath. The tighter fit lends alot to the appearance though and It is true to size. I can understand if you do not like snug fittting clothes you may want to go a size up. If you are like me and do not care for baggy clothes, get your normal size. If you want more room, go a size up.

This jacket it going to make you look good in the colder weather and the lining can be removed in the spring and fall for a lighter jacket. The liner wouldn't look bad as a vest either, perhaps over a hooded sweatshirt.The only thing better would be if the liner had a hood on it for the cold weather as well.

I am actually surprised the first one lasted as long as it did considering the number of times I've pulled it in/out of my pocket, dropped it, banged it, etc.  The durability of this wallet is much better than any other wallet that I've owned.  It's simple, functional, and attracts the attention of a few curious people who are interested about the design and concept.  The quality is terrific.  It holds 5 cards (including driver's license) with ease.  The money clip and cardholder retain their tension, even after repeated use for several years.  The aluminum is strong and resists nicks and scratches.  It is more than what you would normally pay for a wallet but the old adage applies - \\"You get what you pay for.\\"

review_headline: spinner is great but gets stuck in overhead bin
review_body: I own this suitcase and am very happy with the spinner technology (easy to run through airports) and the amount of space in the bag.  However, the design of the front pocket is flawed: it sticks out a bit too much and if you put anything in the inside pouch in the zip-open lid part, the lid sticks out too much and does not fit in the overhead bin of many airplanes (even if you do not expand it or put anything in the outside pockets).  If you always check your bag and don't care about the ability to carry it on, you'll love this suitcase, but if you are like me and will only bring what you can carry onboard the plane, look for another bag.

product_title: Diaper Dude Messenger II Diaper Bag for Dads
review_headline: Lots of pockets but not a lot of room
review_body: We did a lot of research before purchasing this diaper bag. My husband wanted a messenger bag style, since he often is the one carrying it. At first, I really liked the bag. It does have a lot of pockets, which is nice for organizing all the baby stuff. I particularly like the large back pocket, which I now use as a purse for my things, instead of carrying an extra bag.  I felt that, for a newborn, it was a great size with room to spare. However, now that my baby is 7 months old, this diaper bag is not nearly big enough. I should point out that we use cloth diapers, which take up a little more space than disposables. But with 2-3 cloth diapers, the changing pad, nursing cover, extra jacket or blanket for the baby, and a couple of small toys or books, the bag is so full we can't even close the main pocket. Also, after only 6 months of use, the zipper on the main pocket snapped right off, so we can't even close it if we want to now. product_title: Ben Sherman Flap Over Messenger Bag
review_body: This is a genuinely nice looking bag.  If you are concerned about getting a nice looking bag to haul around a few things, and you happen to be 5'10 or less, then may be the perfect bag for you.  To explain, let me list the cons.  If you're still okay with the cons, then this is going to be a fine bag for you.    Cons:    The most glaring thing is how small it is.  If you're looking into other bags, pay attention to the size dimensions of this product.  Specifically, at 3.5 inches wide, it is not going to be capable of holding a ton of stuff.  I bought it to haul a few files or a book and my gadgets to & from work & it works fine for that.  If you're having to haul 3 or more textbooks regularly, I'd strongly advise you to consider other options.    Another weakness is the lack of many compartments.  You have the main compartment, and then you have 3 fairly decent sized zippered compartments (one on the back & one on either side of the front).  There is no dedicated spots for pens, business cards, etc...you just slip put them all into one of the zippered pouches.  Also, the cell phone holder is TINY.
